name: Applied Regression
description: Applied regression studies the fundamentals of models of association of randomly observed outcomes and fixed covariates for the purpose of inference and prediction. Contextual data scientific applications emphasize potential pitfalls and solutions or preventive measures to the pitfalls. Specific inferential models include Normal linear and nonlinear regression for continuous outcomes, logistic regression for binary outcomes and Poisson regression for count outcomes and rates. Real world data applications typically encounter missing data, and hence the course includes definitions and solutions for handling this problem, including imputation. Machine learning models are large data generatlizations of regression models that do not make modeling assumptions and focus primarily on classification or prediction. These models are covered at the end of the course.
prerequisites: Introduction to probability and statistics; R software knowledge and programming
